bibl.title: Direct and indirect influences of executive functions on mathematics achievement

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Domain-specific skills partially mediated the relationship between executive functions and mathematics achievement: Inhibitory control within the numerical domain was associated with factual knowledge and procedural skill, which in turn was associated with mathematical achievement.

span.label: executive function contributions to mathematics achievement
span.quote: In this study we investigated the extent to which executive function skills contribute to these three components of mathematical knowledge, whether this mediates the relationship between executive functions and overall mathematics achievement, and if these relationships change with age.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: Two hundred and ninety-three participants aged between 8 and 25 years completed a large battery of mathematics and executive function tests.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Achievement tests additionally require locating the mathematical problem inside a verbal or visual description and building a problem representation, and working memory maintains and manipulates that representation - which is why a direct working-memory path survives beyond the component skills
span.quote: It is likely that working memory plays a key role in these processes in terms of maintaining and manipulating these problem representations in mind.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Working memory activates and retrieves number facts from long-term memory while inhibition suppresses the neighbouring but incorrect answers that are co-activated during retrieval
span.quote: This is consistent with theories that propose that working memory is required to activate and retrieve mathematical facts stored in long-term memory, and also that inhibitory processes are needed to suppress co-activated but incorrect answers.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Conceptual information is stored in a verbal code whereas arithmetic facts also carry a visuospatial component from how sums are presented and encoded, so only verbal working memory supports conceptual retrieval while both domains support fact retrieval
span.quote: could be because conceptual information is stored in a verbal code, whereas mathematical facts perhaps also contain a visuospatial component

span.label: Because age-appropriate mathematics content was chosen separately for each group, the study may have measured only the application of already-mastered material, which could explain the absence of age-related change.
span.quote: By selecting separate age-appropriate content for the mathematics measures for each group it is possible that we were in fact assessing the role of executive functions in performing and applying already mastered mathematical skills and knowledge in all age groups, and that the role of executive functions in doing this is the same at all ages.

span.label: The direct working-memory-to-achievement pathway has not been shown to survive control for working memory's role in performing the arithmetic operation itself.
span.quote: It remains to be established whether this relationship holds once the role of working memory in performing the appropriate arithmetic operation is taken into account.

span.label: IQ was not included, so its share of the variance in each mathematics component is unknown.
span.quote: Similarly, the role of IQ in explaining variance in each mathematics components has yet to be fully explored.

span.label: The field's existing evidence cannot be put side by side, because it comes from separate studies — which is the stated reason this study exists.
span.quote: However much of this evidence is drawn across separate studies and thus it is not possible to directly compare the contribution of executive functions across these three core competencies of arithmetic.

span.label: The three-part division of the central construct is inherited from one paper rather than derived here.
span.quote: are typically divided into three main components following Miyake et al. (2000).

span.label: a DIFFERENT item set chosen for each age band - 8-9, 11-12, 13-14, and young adults
span.quote: To ensure that performance was not at floor or ceiling level in any group we selected a different set of items for each age group

span.label: the full list of acceptable strategies - counting in the head, on fingers, decomposition, retrieval - stated explicitly to participants
span.quote: to ensure that younger participants understood that any strategy was acceptable in this task

span.label: executive functions
span.quote: are typically divided into three main components following Miyake et al. (2000).

span.label: inhibition
span.quote: (ii) inhibition, the suppression of irrelevant information and inappropriate responses

span.label: shifting
span.quote: (iii) shifting, the capacity for flexible thinking and switching attention between different tasks.

span.label: executive functions - AS DIVIDED HERE: three components following Miyake et al. (2000) — updating or working memory, inhibition, and shifting
span.quote: These are (i) updating or working memory, the ability to monitor and manipulate information held in mind, (ii) inhibition, the suppression of irrelevant information and inappropriate responses, and (iii) shifting, the capacity for flexible thinking and switching attention between different tasks.

span.label: working memory - the Baddeley and Hitch (1974) model, described as adopted by the MAJORITY of researchers in the field rather than as established
span.quote: According to the influential Baddeley and Hitch (1974) model of working memory, adopted by the majority of researchers in this field

span.label: builds-on → Geary (2004); Geary & Hoard (2005) hierarchical framework of mathematics
span.quote: The findings support a modified version of a hierarchical framework for mathematics (Geary, 2004; Geary & Hoard, 2005) in which domain-general executive function skills, in particular working memory, support domain-specific mathematical processes, which in turn underpin overall mathematics achievement.

span.label: extends → previous hierarchical multi-component models of mathematics
span.quote: We extended previous models by demonstrating that working memory also directly contributes to mathematical achievement (Fig. 3).

span.label: contradicts → Cowan and Powell (2014); Fuchs et al. (2005)
span.quote: We found that executive functions explained a similar amount of variance in both factual knowledge (12%) and procedural skill (15%), which is inconsistent with the findings of Cowan and Powell (2014) and Fuchs et al. (2005) who found that domain-general factors accounted for more variance in procedural skill than factual knowledge.

span.label: contradicts → Andersson (2010); Clark et al. (2010)
span.quote: This conflicts with findings from other studies that have examined the extent to which performance on a cognitive flexibility task predicts performance on a test of procedural skill (Andersson, 2010; Clark et al., 2010).

span.label: replicates → Hecht et al. (2003); Jordan et al. (2013)
span.quote: Together the executive function measures predicted more variance in factual knowledge and procedural skill than conceptual understanding, consistent with the findings of Hecht et al., (2003) and Jordan et al. (2013).

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · inhibition —part-of→ executive functions
span.quote: are typically divided into three main components following Miyake et al. (2000). These are (i) updating or working memory, the ability to monitor and manipulate information held in mind, (ii) inhibition, the suppression of irrelevant information and inappropriate responses

span.label: inhibition —part-of→ executive functions
span.quote: The contribution of executive functions, in particular inhibition and shifting, to procedural skill may well depend on age- or schooling-related changes in mathematical content and strategies (Best, Miller, & Naglieri, 2011; Friso-van den Bos et al., 2013; Träff, 2013).

span.label: hierarchical regression
span.quote: To establish that factual knowledge, procedural skill and conceptual understanding all independently contribute to mathematics achievement, we conducted a hierarchical linear regression predicting WIAT mathematics reasoning scores from our measures of factual knowledge, procedural skill and conceptual understanding.

span.label: bootstrap
span.quote: This calculates bias-corrected 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using bootstrapping with 10,000 resamples.

span.label: variance partitioning
span.quote: In order to investigate this, linear regression modelling was used to partition the variance between the storage, processing and central executive components of verbal and visuospatial working memory.

span.label: Mahalanobis distance (outlier detection)
span.quote: were classed as multivariate outliers using Mahalanobis distance and excluded from the study.

span.label: multiple imputation
span.quote: Their missing data (0.3%) was replaced using the multiple imputation option in SPSS.

span.label: standardization (z-scores)
span.quote: We therefore transformed raw scores on all measures to z-scores within each age group and used these in the subsequent analyses.

span.label: descriptive statistics
span.quote: Descriptive statistics for raw performance on the mathematics and executive function tasks are presented in Table 1.

span.label: mediation analysis
span.quote: There were small but significant indirect effects of verbal working memory on mathematics achievement through all three component arithmetic skills; factual knowledge (b = 0.020, 95% CI: 0.005–0.051), procedural skill (b = 0.045, 95% CI: 0.014–0.089) and conceptual understanding (b = 0.015, 95% CI: 0.002–0.041).

span.label: The domain-specific skills of factual knowledge, procedural skill and conceptual understanding only partially mediated the executive-function/achievement link, with numerical inhibitory control acting on achievement through factual knowledge and procedural skill.
span.quote: Domain-specific skills partially mediated the relationship between executive functions and mathematics achievement: Inhibitory control within the numerical domain was associated with factual knowledge and procedural skill, which in turn was associated with mathematical achievement.

span.label: Executive function measures explained far more variance in overall mathematics achievement (34%) than in any single component skill, and least of all in conceptual understanding (5%).
span.quote: As shown in Table 3 the executive function measures alone explained 34% of the variance in mathematical achievement, 12% of the variance in factual knowledge, 15% of the variance in procedural skill and 5% of the variance in conceptual understanding.

span.label: Verbal working memory uniquely predicted all four outcomes - factual knowledge, procedural skill, conceptual understanding and mathematics achievement.
span.quote: Verbal working memory was a unique independent predictor of factual knowledge, procedural skill and conceptual understanding as well as mathematics achievement.

span.label: Set shifting and non-numerical (animal-size Stroop) inhibition predicted nothing once working memory was in the model, whereas numerical inhibition uniquely predicted factual knowledge and procedural skill.
span.quote: Shifting and non-numerical inhibition did not independently predict any of the outcome variables, while numerical inhibition was a unique independent predictor of factual knowledge and procedural skill.

span.label: Contrary to the prediction that executive demands would fall as procedures automatise, the strength of the executive-function/mathematics relationships did not change between 8 years and adulthood.
span.quote: Contrary to our predictions we found that the relationships between executive functions and all components of mathematics were the same from 8 years of age through to adulthood.

span.label: Beyond the indirect routes through the component skills, working memory retained a large direct path to mathematics achievement.
span.quote: There was also a substantial direct effect of visuospatial working memory on mathematics achievement (b = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.15–0.34).

span.label: Verbal working memory influenced achievement indirectly through all three component skills, with the procedural-skill route the largest of the three indirect paths.
span.quote: There were small but significant indirect effects of verbal working memory on mathematics achievement through all three component arithmetic skills; factual knowledge (b = 0.020, 95% CI: 0.005–0.051), procedural skill (b = 0.045, 95% CI: 0.014–0.089) and conceptual understanding (b = 0.015, 95% CI: 0.002–0.041).

span.label: The predicted association of inhibition and shifting with overall mathematics achievement failed to appear when working memory was included in the same model.
span.quote: The predicted relationship between inhibition and shifting and overall mathematics achievement was not found

span.label: executive functions
span.quote: Executive functions, the skills used to guide and control thought and action, are typically divided into three main components following Miyake et al.

span.label: working memory, inhibition and shifting (the three executive components)
span.term: working memory, inhibition and shifting (the three executive components)
span.quote: These are (i) updating or working memory, the ability to monitor and manipulate information held in mind, (ii) inhibition, the suppression of irrelevant information and inappropriate responses, and (iii) shifting, the capacity for flexible thinking and switching attention between different tasks.

span.label: factual knowledge
span.quote: in addition to their factual knowledge: the ability to recall stored number facts from long-term memory

span.label: mathematics achievement (WIAT Mathematics Reasoning)
span.quote: In both models, the mathematics achievement measure was the dependent variable.

span.label: factual knowledge, procedural skill and conceptual understanding
span.term: factual knowledge, procedural skill and conceptual understanding
span.quote: Factual knowledge, procedural skill and conceptual understanding were included as potential mediators and all other executive function measures were included as covariates.

span.label: the other executive function measures
span.quote: Factual knowledge, procedural skill and conceptual understanding were included as potential mediators and all other executive function measures were included as covariates.

span.label: verbal working memory
span.quote: Verbal working memory was a unique independent predictor of factual knowledge, procedural skill and conceptual understanding as well as mathematics achievement.

span.label: age group (dummy-coded contrasts)
span.quote: Interaction terms between the executive function measures and age contrasts were entered in the second step.

span.label: total number of words correctly recalled (verbal short-term memory span)
span.term: total number of words correctly recalled (verbal short-term memory span)
span.quote: The total number of words correctly recalled was used as the dependent variable.

span.label: 293 — total participants tested, aged 8-25 years
span.quote: Two hundred and ninety-three participants aged between 8 and 25 years completed a large battery of mathematics and executive function tests.

span.label: 34% — variance in mathematics achievement explained by the executive function measures alone
span.quote: As shown in Table 3 the executive function measures alone explained 34% of the variance in mathematical achievement, 12% of the variance in factual knowledge, 15% of the variance in procedural skill and 5% of the variance in conceptual understanding.

span.label: b = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.15–0.34 — direct effect of visuospatial working memory on mathematics achievement after the mediators were included
span.quote: There was also a substantial direct effect of visuospatial working memory on mathematics achievement (b = 0.25, 95% CI: 0.15–0.34).

span.label: 9% — unique variance in mathematics achievement attributable to the working memory tasks once storage and processing speed were controlled
span.quote: This contribution was largest for mathematics achievement (9%) followed by procedural skill (2.5–3.5%) and then factual knowledge (1.5%).

span.label: 0.3% — proportion of missing data replaced by multiple imputation
span.quote: Their missing data (0.3%) was replaced using the multiple imputation option in SPSS.
